findings: November raw lines 5-15,32-40 describes Belgium customers using linked card/app and a single-use bank redirect in EUR; immediate payment confirmation is distinct from instant provisional access and the standard payout schedule. Old raw lines 8-38 gave the same basic customer/currency/authentication constraints but labeled the family authenticated bank-debit. The source line 13 compresses these into immediate notification without settlement or provisional-access distinction.

New raw lines 18-40 supply merchant/Connect and B2B/B2C eligibility, account-review caveat, supported business geographies, 0.50 EUR minimum, domestic/cross-border support. Old raw lines 56-99 listed business countries without these qualifiers. Both November business-location lists include GI (new raw lines 19,28), matching the older list (old raw line 75); listed geography alone does not establish a particular account's eligibility.

The material refund deadline changes from 180 days in old raw line 168 and current source lines 13,22 to 730 days/2 years in new raw lines 57-68. New raw lines 68-82 additionally detail full/partial refunds by Dashboard or Refunds API, no cancel after submission, separate bank credit rather than reversal, typically 2-5 days, Refund.status succeeded/failed and refund.updated/refund.failed events, Stripe balance return on failure, and optional bank-transfer reference only after succeeded. Submission, webhook receipt or payment confirmation are not proof of the customer's bank receipt.

New raw lines 63-88 and old raw lines 44-54,162-164 agree no standard chargeback/dispute path; new explanation says bank authentication reduces risk and a customer bank contact routes back to merchant. Current source lines 13,21 say authentication prevents chargebacks categorically; retain the documented standard-dispute scope rather than promising all disputes impossible.

New raw lines 90-116 expand product/API matrix: Checkout full page/embedded form/Payment Links/Payment Element/in-app and Checkout Sessions/Payment Intents supported; Express Checkout, Customer Portal, Terminal, off-session Bancontact, native recurring and manual/partial capture unsupported. Billing and Invoicing are marked supported with send_invoice-only footnote (new raw lines 100-116). Old raw lines 101-111 lists Subscriptions, Invoicing invite-only and Elements with a footnote about ECE and SEPA. Current source line 24 retains old invite-only invoicing as undated current fact and should date it; November matrix does not establish the removal date or account eligibility.

New raw lines 41-42,109-114 mark native Bancontact recurring, Payment Intents with setup_future_usage and Setup Intents unsupported. Old raw lines 32-34 and current source lines 13,20 explain recurring via SEPA Direct Debit; separate May raw stripe-bancontact-set-up-payment-2025.md lines 16-28,50-85 and stripe-bancontact-save-during-payment-2025.md lines 12-16,49-64 explicitly describe SetupIntent or Bancontact PaymentIntent setup_future_usage flows that generate a SEPA Debit PaymentMethod. This is a genuine cross-page apparent conflict requiring reciprocal dated warning, not grounds to erase the older SEPA setup guides or infer all Bancontact saving is impossible.

New raw lines 117-141 turn old raw lines 113-141 illustrated card/QR flows into six prose steps; it adds a one-hour bank authentication window (new raw line 133) and says automatic return after authorization (new raw line 141) whereas old flow calls return optional (old raw lines 126,141). Record the return wording divergence, and do not use browser return as proof of payment success; the guide says immediate success/failure notification at new raw line 137.

New raw lines 143-147 add non-card statement_descriptor rather than card-only suffix and Connect destination-charge default platform descriptor unless on_behalf_of names connected account. New raw lines 149-155 retain Dashboard method enabling from old raw lines 143-159 and add active bancontact_payments capability prerequisite for connected accounts using Express/no hosted Dashboard. Neither method setting nor requested capability proves account eligibility or a successful charge.

Main concept route is wiki/index.md lines 5-7 to wiki/stripe-index.md lines 267,750 to wiki/concepts/stripe-bancontact.md lines 8-43. The Stripe index line 267 and concept line 19 both repeat the old 180-day refund window; line 20 repeats old invite-only invoicing; lines 18,40-43 link SEPA saving guides, making dated reciprocal warning necessary. Related bank-redirect concept lines 16-34 separately says Bancontact SetupIntents/setup_future_usage yes and send_invoice subscription support.

Source-schema issue separate from the raw delta: wiki/sources/source-stripe-bancontact.md frontmatter lines 1-9 lacks canonical_url. The mapped source should carry the trusted exact canonical identity https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bancontact under rules/ingest-roles.md source schema; its absence does not imply a Bancontact behavior change.

New eligibility/support matrix adds 0.50 EUR minimum, account review and Connect capability caveats, product/API matrix, capture/authorization exclusions, and send_invoice-only Billing/Invoicing context (new raw lines 18-61,90-116,149-155 versus old raw lines 14-111,143-160).

source_assessments.reason: The overview now supplies material new refund, eligibility, status, support and descriptor details, while the source and main Stripe index refund deadline is stale. Preserve dated May claims, flag unresolved setup/save, Invoicing and return-wording boundaries, and add the required missing canonical URL metadata.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bancontact, new raw lines 5-40 and 90-155 describe a single-use Belgian-customer, EUR Bancontact bank redirect with immediate success/failure confirmation, standard payout timing, a 0.50 EUR minimum, merchant/Connect eligibility and an active bancontact_payments capability for certain connected accounts. Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents may accept it, but native recurring, off-session Bancontact, manual capture and standard chargebacks are unsupported. Full or partial refunds have a 730-day submission window and reach a bank as a separate credit, with succeeded/failed Refund status distinct from submission (new raw lines 57-82). The old raw lines 8-54 and 162-168 had the same basic flow but a 180-day refund window. source-stripe-bancontact.md and wiki/stripe-index.md line 267 still state 180 days; the source also has an undated invite-only Invoicing gate and lacks the trusted canonical URL, so it requires dated and metadata corrections.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/bancontact, the 180-to-730-day refund change is substantive (old raw lines 166-168; new raw lines 57-82), as are new eligibility, support, status, one-hour authentication, descriptor and Connect capability details. The old image-led payment flow becoming six prose steps is presentation, though old raw lines 126-141 call merchant return optional and new raw lines 131-141 call it automatic. source-stripe-bancontact.md and wiki/stripe-index.md line 267 must correct their stale 180-day route; the source must also add its missing canonical URL, preserve dated May SEPA-mediated recurring and invite-only Invoicing claims, and record November's native-recurring/setup exclusions and send_invoice-only matrix. Separate May Bancontact-to-SEPA SetupIntent and setup_future_usage guides conflict with new raw lines 112-114, so no blanket removal or compatibility claim is proven. Refund submission is not bank receipt, a browser return is not payment proof, and account eligibility is not established by a country list alone.
